messages:
rachael_cs: Quick flag - Lighthouse renewal blocked: finance needs EU invoice to subsidiary but procurement says vendor code required. Customer prefers card. Need decision by Tue COB or they slip month.

 tom_sales: They asked for 9-month term with 10% concession in exchange for earlier sign. Also requested two enablement sessions during rollout.

 ivy_proc: PO route requires VAT ID + remit address + legal entity exact name. Card route needs cardholder auth + fraud review (~24h). Which path are they leaning?

 omar_legal: We need an EU invoicing clause: "Customer responsible for VAT where applicable; Redwood will invoice based on entity provided." Also include no-auto-renew language. Legal ok otherwise.

 pricing-team: Pricing note: 9-month term -> apply 8% uplift. If they prepay, reduce uplift by 5%. Need seat count + token estimate before finalizing.

 rachael_cs: Customer sent VAT and remit: Lighthouse Europe SARL, VAT LT123456789, 12 Rue du Port, 75001 Paris. They prefer SEPA monthly but will provide card as backup.

 ivy_proc: SEPA monthly accepted; procurement still needs remit docs to create vendor code. Please send to procurement@redwood.com and we'll queue vendor-code; turnaround ~36-48h once validated.

 esign-bot: DocuSign envelope created: Lighthouse Renewal (SOW_v3) - awaiting signer: pierre@lighthouse.eu

 rachael_cs: TL;DR: Lighthouse chooses EU entity monthly SEPA, VAT provided, vendor-code in progress, pricing pending seat counts. Target: close by Wed. :shipit:
